extracted.intended_audience: CPSC staff, rulewriters, regulated firms (manufacturers/private labelers), and legal counsel/stakeholders participating in notice-and-comment and disclosure procedures under section 6(b) of the CPSA
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of evaluation/implementation criteria for the Commission's public disclosure rules under section 6(b) of the CPSA (16 CFR part 1101), including when notice/comment is required or excused, reasonable steps for accuracy and fairness, exceptions, retraction, and treatment of section 15(b) submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances when the Commission does not provide notice and opportunity to comment (§1101.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances when notice and opportunity to comment is not practicable include, but are not necessarily limited to, specified situations (revised language proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed examples to add: (1) When the Commission has been unable, after a diligent search, to obtain contact information for the manufacturer or private labeler of the consumer product to which the information pertains; (2) When an extraordinary circumstance necessitates the immediate disclosure of information to protect the public health and safety while the Commission simultaneously pursues notification of the manufacturer or private labeler. Staff conducts thorough searches in internal databases and other sources; emergency example: a holiday weekend hazard where attempts to contact the firm go unanswered. Even when notice is not practicable, consistent with section 6(b)(1) the Commission would take reasonable steps to assure information is accurate and that disclosure is fair and reasonably related to effectuating the Acts' purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of comments (§1101.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: In disclosing any information under this section, the Commission may, and upon the written request of the manufacturer or private labeler shall, include any comments or other information or a summary thereof submitted by the manufacturer or private labeler, to the extent permitted by and subject to the requirements of section 6 of the CPSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed change requires all requests regarding disclosure of a manufacturer's or private labeler's comments to be in writing. The revision conforms the rule to the statute and creates an affirmative written-request mechanism for including or limiting inclusion of firms' comments in disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosing materially more or materially different information (§1101.31(d) → (c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission intends to disclose information, not previously disclosed, that in context does not disclose materially more or materially different information about the consumer product than what the Commission previously disclosed in accordance with the law, the Commission is not obligated to take any additional steps to assure accuracy unless the Commission has reason to question the accuracy of the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: if prior notice-and-comment addressed the substance of the disclosure, repeating the process would not advance section 6(b) purposes. However, if accuracy is called into question, additional steps must be taken. This replaces a more verbose prior provision about re-reviewing previously disclosed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory statement is discretionary (revised §1101.31 / §1101.32 linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is not required under section 6(b)(1) to provide an explanatory statement with information it discloses to the public; an explanatory statement may be referenced in §1101.32 as a possible step to assure accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed edits remove mandatory or presumptive language (e.g., 'Where appropriate', 'will', 'To the extent practicable') and change wording to 'may' to reflect that an explanatory statement is optional. The explanatory statement may be used in §1101.32(b) as one of the measures to assure accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to assure information is accurate (§1101.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must take reasonable steps to assure, prior to disclosing information, that such information is accurate. §1101.32 specifies actions considered to be reasonable steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed/explicit reasonable steps include: (a) Commission staff or a qualified person/entity conducts an investigation (the term 'investigation' is broad and encompasses inspections); (b) reliance on a statement made under oath or a statement enforceable under penalty of perjury (e.g., 28 U.S.C. 1746) that yields or corroborates the information; (c) the person who submitted the information confirms it as accurate to the best of their knowledge and belief, subject to conditions. The rule deletes an explicit sentence giving more weight to specific comments than general comments, and a new paragraph (b) would allow use of an explanatory statement to help assure accuracy. Technical and grammatical conforming edits are proposed throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to assure information release is fair in the circumstances (§1101.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: §1101.33(a) enumerates actions that constitute reasonable steps to assure disclosure is fair in the circumstances; revisions clarify and conform to statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key proposed revisions: (1) When a firm requests non-disclosure of its comments, the firm must provide a basis (not necessarily a legal rationale) and such requests must be in writing; (2) The Commission may, but is not required to, accompany disclosure with an explanatory statement and may disclose other relevant information in its possession to assure fairness, subject to section 6(b)(1) and other law; (3) delete obsolete guidance limiting the geographic form of disclosure (internet posting makes geographic limits generally obsolete); (4) delete an example authorizing delay of disclosure as unnecessary. §1101.33(b) changes: deletion of the prior presumption that attorney work-product and attorney-client privileged materials are categorically inappropriate for disclosure (Commission believes firms generally waive protections by voluntarily submitting such materials), but firms may request confidentiality under FOIA rules for trade secrets/confidential commercial info; revised treatment of disclosure of firm's comments — firm must provide some basis why comments should not be disclosed and Commission has broad discretion whether to grant non-disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure must be reasonably related to effectuating the purposes of the Acts (§1101.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(1) requires the Commission to take reasonable steps to assure that disclosure is reasonably related to effectuating the purposes of the CPSA, FFA, PPPA, and FHSA; §1101.34 is conformed to reflect that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed conforming changes remove references to acts other than the listed statutes and delete §1101.34(a)(3) (which had addressed FOIA requests and deferred to FOIA in close questions) because FOIA is not one of the enumerated Acts in section 6(d)(1). However, the Commission must still comply with section 6(b) before disclosing information in response to FOIA. The heading edits replace 'release' with 'disclosure' and clarify references to 'consumer products.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exceptions scope (§1101.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory exceptions of section 6(b)(4) apply specifically to the CPSA, FHSA, FFA, and PPPA; the regulation formats and lists the types of disclosures covered by the exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed conforming revisions insert 'Acts' to clarify the exceptions' scope, remove duplicative paragraph about 'transferred acts', and reformat paragraphs (a)(3) and (a)(4) into a combined list stating exceptions apply to information in the course of or concerning: (i) rulemaking proceedings under the Acts; (ii) adjudicatory proceedings under the Acts; or (iii) any other administrative or judicial proceeding under the Acts. Removal of paragraph designations/subheadings is proposed to reflect deletions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imminent hazard exception scope (§1101.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: The imminent hazard exception applies once the Commission has filed an action under section 12 of the CPSA in a U.S. district court, permitting disclosure of information concerning the product alleged to be imminently hazardous without following section 6(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed revisions remove limiting phrases (e.g., 'while the proceeding is pending') and delete sentences to reflect the Commission's view that upon filing a section 12 action, information may be disclosed during and after the proceeding even if not filed with the court or otherwise made public. Conforming changes and minor grammatical edits are proposed; the provision distinguishes information already made public from information retained by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable cause to believe standard (§1101.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission interprets 'reasonable cause to believe' as existing when the belief is supported by existing laws and regulations and is based on factual conclusions that have evidentiary support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative examples: reasonable cause exists where Commission testing indicates a toy contains excessive lead, staff confirms lack of required General Conformity Certification, or staff determines a manufacturer is distributing ATVs without a required ATV Action Plan. The Commission will notify a manufacturer or private labeler orally or in writing if it has reasonable cause to believe a product violates a safety rule or statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking proceeding exception interpretation (§1101.44)
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'concerning' for the rulemaking proceeding exception is interpreted broadly to mean 'about, addressing, relating to' the proceeding, and the Commission may publicly disclose information that describes or relates to the substance, process, or outcome of the proceeding at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed text inserts 'or addressing' and 'or relates to' to reflect that 'concerning' should be understood broadly. Examples: Commissioners and presiding officials acting as decisionmakers may publicly explain votes and decisions by issuing opinions and public statements. Conforming and grammatical edits are proposed for simplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudicatory proceeding exception interpretation (§1101.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'concerning' for adjudicatory proceedings is similarly interpreted broadly: information about or addressing the administrative adjudication, both once it begins and indefinitely thereafter, may be disclosed at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised §1101.45(d) states the Commission may disclose information that describes or relates to the substance, process, or outcome of the proceeding. Examples: Commissioners may explain votes via opinions/statements; the Commission may disclose effectiveness of corrective action (e.g., number of products corrected). Proposed edits include conforming language to the statute (e.g., clarifying adjudicatory proceeding 'shall commence upon issuance of a complaint').

rubrics_metrics.name: Other administrative or judicial proceeding exception (§1101.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings included in the 'other administrative or judicial proceeding' exception are illustrative and not exhaustive; interpret 'in the course of or concerning' consistently with §§1101.44/1101.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed deletion of a sentence that would have been excessively restrictive (describing petition proceedings' subject matter in narrow terms). The NPR proposes inserting 'without limitation' to clarify lists are illustrative, and revising §1101.46(c) to cross-reference the interpretation of 'in the course of or concerning' from §§1101.44(c)/(d) and 1101.45(c)/(d) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction procedure and requirements (§1101.51–1101.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission finds it has made public disclosure of inaccurate or misleading information that reflects adversely upon safety of a product/class or practices of manufacturers/private labelers/distributors/retailers, it shall, in a manner equivalent to that in which such disclosure was made, take reasonable steps to publish a retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed alignment with statute: limit requester classes to manufacturers, private labelers, distributors, retailers (delete 'any other person'); require request to include identity and relationship of requester; update contact information and allow reproduction of the disclosure (image/audio/video/copy) to accompany the request 'if practicable'; if equivalent publication is not practicable or could result in further disclosure of the information (e.g., staff disclosed inaccurate info in a phone call or email), the Commission will publish a retraction or take other appropriate action consistent with section 6(b)(7). Proposed deletion of duplicative language and various minor clarifying edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information submitted pursuant to section 15(b) — disclosure criteria (§1101.61)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 6(b)(5), the Commission shall not disclose to the public information that has been identified as submitted pursuant to section 15(b) and 16 CFR 1115.13, except in specified instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed revisions: delete language that treated staff characterization as controlling and instead rely on the filer's own characterization (absent exceptional circumstances); require the submitting firm to identify the information as submitted pursuant to section 15(b) and 16 CFR 1115.13; delete a sentence that extended section 6(b)(5) to voluntary information submitted after the initial report. The NPR proposes to clarify the four instances where the limitation does not apply, including adding 'corrective action plan' and 'consent order' as examples of remedial settlement agreements where disclosure limitations do not apply; redesignate paragraph about a submitter agreeing to public disclosure.
